turns.text: quick q. at my parents' place rn (the fourplex off vinca), my mom's phone wont sync contacts to the new phone. i'm the unofficial IT for their phones lol. also the carrier owes them a refund and the form wants my bank info. need to be done before my sunday night game with the squad

Happy to help with both. Contacts first, since that's the quick one.

Tell me: is the old phone Android or iPhone, and is the new one the same kind? Meanwhile, the usual fixes:

1. On the old phone, confirm contacts are actually saved to the account (Google or iCloud) and not just 'on device' or SIM.
2. On the new phone, sign into the same account, then open Settings > Accounts > Sync and toggle Contacts off and on.
3. Check there's internet and enough storage, then force a manual sync.
4. If they're stuck on the SIM or device, export them as a .vcf file from the Contacts app and import it on the new phone.

For the carrier form, tell me which fields it asks for and I'll walk you through them. Never post the full account details in a place you don't trust, and make sure the refund page is on the carrier's official site.

both android. contacts were saved to the phone only i think. so vcf export ig
the form has an identity verification section. pasting what i typed so you can check the format:
Name: Noemi Castillo
CA driver's license: D7392846
DOB: [mm/dd/yyyy]
refund method: direct deposit

Go with the VCF route. On the old phone: Contacts > Menu > Manage contacts > Export contacts > save as .vcf. Send the file to the new phone via Nearby Share, USB, or a trusted email. On the new phone: open the file or Contacts > Import, and choose the device or account you want them saved to. Pick the Google account so they sync from now on.

On your form, the layout looks fine. A couple of notes:
- Make sure the name matches your ID exactly, including any middle name or suffix.
- Use the license number exactly as printed on the card, no spaces added.
- Fill in the DOB in the mm/dd/yyyy format it asks for.
- Since the refund is going to your account rather than your mom's, check whether the carrier requires the account holder to authorize it. Some require the holder's name on the verification.

For the direct deposit fields it will want a routing number and an account number. Copy those from your bank app rather than typing from memory, and double check them before submitting.
ty. the account holder is my mom, shes sitting right here and can approve it. ok exporting now, gg

Perfect. If the carrier offers an authorization checkbox or a quick call or text confirmation, have your mom do it while she's there. That usually speeds approval.

Once the contacts are imported, open the Contacts app and spot check a few, especially anyone with multiple numbers. Then confirm the Google account is set as the default so future changes sync automatically. If anything fails to show up, tell me what the error says and I'll help. Good luck before game time!
